subject: Post-call: Nimbus throughput & latency validation — next tests
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@nebula-ai.com>, Eric Lin <eric.lin@hypercloud.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Nimbus throughput & latency validation — next tests

Hi Danielle / Eric —

Thanks for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the performance validation: 

Call highlights
- Objective: validate p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec for your in-prod prompt mix and compare Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler-managed endpoints.
- Key metrics you care about: p50/p95/p99 latency, steady-state tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens under typical concurrency.
- Constraints: sequence lengths up to 1,024, occasional 2,048 spikes; strong preference for p99 < 800ms for 1k seq at 8 concurrent requests.

Proposed immediate actions (short timeline):
1) Shared benchmark config: we attached a starting benchmark-config.yaml that codifies prompt mix, seq-length distribution, concurrency sweep, and reporting fields. Please review by Wed 8/25.
2) Token sample: you provided a short sample of your requests; we used tokens-sample.txt to set realistic tokenization.
3) A/B test plan: run a 48-hour A/B against Hyperscaler-API and Redwood-Dedicated with identical request streams:
   - Workload: 10k requests/hour, sampled to match your production distribution
   - Configs: batching disabled / batching=auto / 8k-batch simulation (we'll iterate)
   - Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU-util, request queue time, tail latency breakdown
4) Ownership: Redwood will spin up the Dedicated pool and provide a signed short-lived test token. Nimbus will run the Hyperscaler side or provide access for Redwood to run both.
5) Reporting: we'll populate redwood-vs-hyperscaler-result-template.xlsx and share results.

Can you confirm: (a) you can share Hyperscaler endpoint credentials or let us run both sides, (b) acceptance criteria (p99 <= 800ms vs target), and (c) access window you prefer next week?

I'll schedule a 30-min check-in after the first 6 hours of the run for quick triage.

Thanks —
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: benchmark-config.yaml (text), tokens-sample.txt (text), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-result-template.xlsx (sheet)
From: Danielle Park <dpark@nebula-ai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eric Lin <eric.lin@hypercloud.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Nimbus throughput & latency validation — next tests

Kim —

Thanks for the clear write-up. We can do the A/B run next Tue/Wed (8/24-8/25) in your proposed window. A few clarifications:
- We will host the Hyperscaler side and can provide an API key for Redwood read-only test access if you need to kick off both sides. Prefer to share credentials via our SFTP vault; I can put them there by EOD Mon.
- Acceptance: p99 < 800ms is our preferred bar, but we also want a comparison against cost per 1M tokens. If costs are within 15% and tail wins, that's a big plus.
- For batching, we want the run to include a no-batching baseline and then a realistic batching profile reflecting our bursty traffic.

I'll upload a 1k-entry sample of production prompts (redacted) to the Drive link and confirm credential delivery.

Best,
Danielle

--
Danielle Park
Head of Platform | Nimbus AI
dpark@nebula-ai.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nimbus benchmarks — test harness details

Kim / Connor —

Forwarding notes from our infra sync about how we'll run the sweep. Key points:
- We'll deploy a lightweight harness in the Nimbus VPC (or our staging env if they provide keys) using k6 for request patterns and a small collector that pushes metrics to Prometheus + Grafana.
- We'll record exact model checkpoints, quantization (fp16 vs 4-bit), and kernel flags; log KV cache usage to explain occasional tail spikes.
- Default test matrix for the first pass: seq=[256,1024,2048], concurrency=[1,4,8], batching=[0,auto], model-family=[redwood-v1-7b-q4f, hypercloud-7b-fp16].
- We'll produce a results CSV and fill the provided XLSX template.

I'll pick up infra provisioning Tuesday morning and will need an ops contact at Nimbus if we need to access the Hyperscaler endpoint directly.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference

- Karthik & Connor will be on standby for infra and troubleshooting during 8/24 10:00–18:00 PT (we'll actually start the run at 10:30).
- We can accept Hyperscaler credentials via your SFTP vault. Please send the vault pointer and notify me when the key is there.
- Attached is the initial benchmark-config.yaml with the exact timing windows and monitoring endpoints. 

Looking forward — we'll populate the XLSX as we go and share an interim report after 6 hours.

Best,
Kim

Kim —

SFTP pointer sent to your inbox (separate secure note). We approved the run window and our ops contact (Lena Ortiz) will join the check-in. Lena will also confirm when the Hyperscaler key is live in the vault.

Acceptance criteria reminder: if p99 is within 800ms AND cost delta <= 15% in Redwood's favor, we'll prioritize Redwood for our next pilot. If Hyperscaler wins tail but cost is >20% cheaper, we'll request a follow-up optimization pass.

See you tomorrow morning for the kickoff.

Danielle
